claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex

circumstances: Child is not in local authority care

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning an assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child/children.

**How old is your child (or your youngest child if you have multiple children)?**

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation:
- **Under 16**: Generally automatic qualification
- **16-19**: Need to check if they're in education or training
- **20 or older**: Would not be a qualifying child for Child Benefit

Please tell me:
1. How many children are you claiming for?
2. What is their age (or ages)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Thanks for helping me with this.

I have one child - Alex is 8 years old, so well under 16. We live together here in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Wonderful! Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old and you live together in the UK. That's great - Alex clearly falls into the "under 16" category, which is a good starting point.

Let me navigate through the eligibility requirements for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now let me ask you the next question:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

Given that Alex is only 8 years old, I'd assume the answer is no - Alex isn't in paid work - but I need to confirm this for the assessment. This is a standard eligibility check to ensure the child isn't working full-time, which would affect eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all - he's only 8! He's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I'd expect for an 8-year-old. Alex isn't working at all and is in primary school. Let me continue through the eligibility checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Here's the next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

In other words, Alex doesn't have their own benefit claim - they would just be a dependent on your household claim, correct? At 8 years old, this should be straightforward, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is simply a child living at home with you, no benefits in their own name. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Here's the next check:

**Is Alex NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?**

Given that Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, I'd assume he's not in any apprenticeship at all. But I need to ask to be thorough: Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship programme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8 and still in primary school! No apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - Alex is 8 and in primary school, so definitely not in any apprenticeship. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we're at an important check - **residency requirements**. This is a key eligibility criterion for Child Benefit.

You mentioned earlier that you and Alex live together in the UK. Let me confirm your residency situation:

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

This is the most common path. If yes, that would satisfy the residency requirement. However, I should also ask in case there are any special circumstances:

- Are you a UK national living in the UK?
- Or do you have any immigration status I should know about (such as settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a Crown servant living abroad)?

Please let me know your residency situation so I can confirm you meet the requirements.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I'm a UK resident living here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward - you normally live in the UK and you're a UK resident. That clearly satisfies the residency requirement. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now we're at the responsibility check. The question is:

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

Responsibility for Child Benefit means either:
1. **You live with the child** - which you've already told me you do, or
2. **You contribute to their upkeep** - paying for things like food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc., or
3. **You're paying maintenance** - under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned you live together with Alex, you clearly meet the first criterion. Just to confirm - you and Alex live in the same household together, correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives with me at home. We share the same household.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You and Alex share the same household - that clearly establishes responsibility. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to ask about multiple claimants:

**Is there anyone else who is claiming (or might be claiming) Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent also claiming for him?
- Is anyone else in a different household claiming for him?
- Are there any disputes about who should be the claimant?

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm the only one claiming for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So you're the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex - there's no other claimant and no disputes. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now let me ask about Alex's current living situation:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

Specifically:
- Is Alex in hospital?
- Is Alex in a care home or residential care?
- Is Alex being fostered?
- Or is Alex living at home with you normally?

This helps determine if any special duration rules apply.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living at home with me normally - not in hospital, not in care, and not being fostered. Just a regular home situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living at home with you in a normal household situation. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost at the final check. Here's the last question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, you're covering Alex's living costs (housing, food, care, etc.) yourself rather than having the local council pay for these things. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct. The local council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance - I cover all his living costs myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final piece of the puzzle. You cover all of Alex's living costs yourself, and the local council isn't paying for his accommodation or maintenance. Let me navigate to the outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Wonderful news! 🎉

## You are **ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit!

Based on the assessment, you meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's a summary of why:

**Your Eligibility Summary:**
- ✅ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- ✅ Alex is not working full-time
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✅ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You normally live in the UK (residency requirement met)
- ✅ You are responsible for Alex (live together)
- ✅ You are the only claimant for Alex
- ✅ Alex is living at home with you normally
- ✅ The local council is not paying towards Alex's living costs

**Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate**
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may face a charge that reduces the benefit
5. **Payment schedule** - payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can find more information and apply at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Congratulations! Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's brilliant, thank you so much for your help! That's all very clear. I'll go ahead and apply online then. Thanks again!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm so glad I could help. You have a straightforward case, and you should have no problem with your application. Good luck with claiming Child Benefit for Alex - I hope the process goes smoothly for you!

If you have any other questions in the future about Child Benefit or need any clarification, feel free to ask. Best of luck! 👋

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Your eligibility assessment has been recorded. Wishing you all the best with your Child Benefit application! 🌟

All eligibility criteria have been met.
